Implementation Plan

Plan for issue #6403: stop a failing check's name from injecting routing lines into the triage issue

Planning ref: `git rev-parse HEAD` = `aaadeb9a5abd243aa75797d0ca0ce99b81b6d0cc`, branch `claude/ci-failure-triage-workflow-run`. This matches the Integration branch metadata, so there is no mismatch.

## Automation surface (§20.E)
- This only changes existing code. No new script, scheduled job, long-running process or DB work, and nothing to add to `docs/scripts-pending-removal.md`.
- The change runs through the existing `check_run` / `workflow_run` triggers. These call `.github/workflows/check_failure_triage.yml`, which runs `scripts/check_failure_triage.sh` and then the "Post check-failure triage issue" step.

Scope-mode: Hold Scope
Reuse-audit: extends scripts/check_failure_triage.sh routing-metadata neutralizer
Scope-mode justification: The finding is an injection at one entry point. The check name is untrusted (with `workflow_run` it is the workflow's YAML `name:` from the PR head; with `check_run` it is any app's check name). It reaches the triage issue header, the issue title, prompt lines and log/Telegram lines without being cleaned. The script already has a neutralizer for log and model text. It just doesn't cover the header the script writes itself. The full fix is about 30 lines of shell and Python plus tests: clean the name once, at the source, inside the trusted script and the reusable workflow. That also covers both consumer wrappers and the internal wrapper without a consumer sync. The recommendation's second half (make `scripts/resolve_integration_ref.sh` read routing only from provenance-checked fields) would change routing for every issue type. Security-audit issues like this one legitimately use a body `Integration branch:` line. That part is out of scope here (see D2).

## Conflict / grounding notes
- The finding cites `workflow-templates/ai-check-failure-triage.yml:69`, which is `check_name: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.name }}`. That location is correct. `.github/workflows/internal-check-failure-triage.yml:58` has the same forwarding.
- Injection points confirmed in `scripts/check_failure_triage.sh`:
  - line 522: `- **Failing check:** \`${CHECK_NAME}\`` in the issue header. This is written after the diagnosis neutralizer runs (lines 484-504), so nothing cleans it.
  - line 508: `TITLE=`
  - line 406: the prompt's `Failing check: ${CHECK_NAME}` line, which sits outside any UNTRUSTED fence
  - log lines 159/165/174/264/279/570/575, where a newline lets the name start a new stdout line such as `::warning::…`
  - Telegram lines 286/571/576
- In `.github/workflows/check_failure_triage.yml` (around line 459) the post step builds `--title "CI failure: ${CHECK_NAME} …"` from the raw input. It strips CR/LF only afterwards, for the log and Telegram lines.

## Files likely to change
1. `scripts/check_failure_triage.sh`
2. `.github/workflows/check_failure_triage.yml` (post step only)
3. `tests/test_check_failure_triage_workflow_security.py`
4. `agents.md` (one clause in pipeline item 13, "check failure triage")
5. `changelog.d/6403-triage-check-name-neutralize.md` (new)

No changes to `workflow-templates/ai-check-failure-triage.yml` or `internal-check-failure-triage.yml`. Workflow expressions can't sanitize text, and fixing it centrally covers every caller (D1).

## Functions / modules to implement
A. `scripts/check_failure_triage.sh`
- Add a function `sanitize_check_name_display` (Allman braces, tabs). It passes its argument as argv to `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -c` and prints one line:
  1. Replace every character whose `unicodedata.category` starts with `C` (Cc, Cf, Cs, Co, Cn), or is `Zl`/`Zp`, with a space. This covers `\r`, `\n`, `\x85`, U+2028/U+2029 and bidi/zero-width characters.
  2. Collapse runs of whitespace to one space and strip the ends.
  3. Replace backticks with `'` so the name can't close the code span.
  4. Replace `<` with `<` so the name can't open a marker comment like `<!-- ai:… -->` or `<!-- check-failure-triage:… -->`.
  5. Apply the same routing-key rewrite as the diagnosis neutralizer: the keys `integration branch`, `target branch`, `tracking issue`, `depends on`, `local id`, `managed by`, `prior_pr_baseline_branch`, `files_touched` followed by `:` become `<key> (untrusted):`. Also rewrite `Re-issued from #` and `review-blocked-reissue` the same way. This is defense in depth in case the name ever ends up at the start of a line.
  6. Truncate to 200 characters, matching the workflow's existing `safe_check_name` limit.
  7. If the result is empty, print `(unnamed check)`.
  - Implementation note: put the key tuple and regexes in the function's Python and keep them identical to the diagnosis block, with a comment saying the two lists must stay in sync. Don't refactor the existing heredoc (§9).
- Call it once, right after the `if [ "${TRIAGE_STAGE}" = "diagnose" ] … fi` metadata-load block (after line 141), so every stage sets `CHECK_NAME_DISPLAY` before its first use. Fail closed: if the helper exits non-zero, log `error check_name_sanitize_failed` (without the name) and `exit 1`.
- Switch every rendered use to `CHECK_NAME_DISPLAY`: log lines 159, 165, 174, 264, 279, 570, 575; Telegram 286, 571, 576; prompt line 406; `TITLE` at 508; body header 522.
- Keep raw `CHECK_NAME` in four places:
  - the `FP=` fingerprint (line 181), so dedup keys stay the same and `tests/test_ci_failure_workflow_run_triggers.py:118` stays green
  - the self-loop `case` match (line 172)
  - the `check_name` field in `triage_metadata.json` (line 309)
  - the workflow's concurrency hash
- Move the prompt's `Failing check:` line inside the existing `BEGIN/END UNTRUSTED PR title` fence, renamed in the echo text to `PR title and check name`. Do this only if no test pins the fence text; otherwise keep the fence text and just use the display value.

B. `.github/workflows/check_failure_triage.yml`, step "Post check-failure triage issue"
- Compute `triage_post_check_name` before `gh issue create`. Keep the existing CR/LF substitutions and add `${triage_post_check_name//[[:cntrl:]]/ }` plus a `:0:200` cap. Use it in `--title` instead of the raw `${CHECK_NAME}`. The log and Telegram lines already use that variable.
- Only the step body changes. `name:`, `if:` and `env:` stay as they are (§10/§24). Check the file size with `wc -c`; it is a 490-line file, far below 480,000 bytes.

## Data structures affected
- `triage_metadata.json`: no schema change. `check_name` stays raw.
- Issue body header: only the rendered `Failing check` value changes. The `check-failure-triage:` markers and their order don't change, so the post step's first-line marker validation still holds.

## API / interface changes
- None. No new env vars or inputs, and no extra GitHub API calls (§14).
- Visible differences: for names with control characters, backticks or `<`, the issue title and header now show the cleaned name. Ordinary names are unchanged.

## Decisions
### D1 — Where to clean the check name
- Chosen: clean it inside the trusted `scripts/check_failure_triage.sh` and the reusable workflow's post step, and keep the raw name only for hashing and dedup.
- Alternatives considered: (a) change the consumer and internal wrappers to forward a different field such as `workflow.path`; (b) reject names that contain newlines and skip triage.
- Why: (a) needs a consumer sync, still leaves `check_run` names from third-party apps open, and would change the fingerprint and dedup grouping. (b) would quietly drop real CI failures. Cleaning at the shared trusted layer fixes every caller at once and keeps behaviour the same for normal names.

### D2 — The resolver-side provenance recommendation
- Chosen: leave `scripts/resolve_integration_ref.sh` as it is and document this.
- Alternatives considered: make the resolver accept `Integration branch:` only from trusted authors or structured fields.
- Why: the resolver is shared by security-audit issues (including this one), orchestrator children and review-blocked reissues. They all legitimately set routing through the body line, so changing it is cross-cutting and breaks existing routing. The triage script is the only writer that put untrusted text into its header, and that is what this change fixes. A resolver provenance check can be a separate issue.

### D3 — Keep the raw name in the fingerprint
- Chosen: `FP` and the concurrency key keep hashing the raw name.
- Alternatives considered: hash the cleaned name.
- Why: hashing the cleaned name would change dedup keys for existing open triage issues and break a pinned contract test. Two hostile names that clean to the same text would still get separate fingerprints, which is harmless.

## Security considerations
- Trust boundaries:
  - `inputs.check_name` comes from either the PR head's workflow YAML `name:` (a same-repo PR author controls it) or a third-party check app.
  - The issue body is trusted routing input for `resolve_integration_ref.sh`, `security_dependency.py` (`Depends on:`) and `orchestrate_lib.py` (`TARGET_BRANCH_LINE_RE`).
  - The issue is posted with `CHECK_TRIAGE_ISSUES_TOKEN`, and the resulting `issues: opened` event starts clarify, then plan and implement with the resolved ref.
- Authorization: no new surface. The existing `same_repo` gate and the token split stay as they are.
- Input validation: control and line-separator characters, backticks, `<`, routing keys and length are all handled before the name is rendered anywhere.
- Abuse cases covered:
  1. A multiline workflow `name:` containing `Integration branch: stable`, which would otherwise route the triage fix to an attacker-chosen branch.
  2. A name containing `- Depends on: #N`, which would put a security dependency hold on the issue.
  3. A name containing `<!-- check-failure-triage:gen=0 -->`, which would reset the lineage cap.
  4. A name containing ``` ` ``` that closes the code span and injects markdown.
